objet: Engagement letters, and the whole engagement moved to euros
disponibilite: I remain available to answer any question on these terms.

corps.p: Thank you for your confirmation. Please find enclosed the two engagement letters.

Your message of the same day raised a second matter, quite separate from the Valais tax line. Inheritance tax paid out of your father's estate on assets situated in France which were never received, and an apartment in Neuilly-sur-Seine whose fate is unknown to you. That is a different estate, in a different country, and it needs its own mandate. Hence two letters rather than one.

The first covers the Swiss matters, at EUR 7,500 excluding tax per month. The second covers the French matters, at EUR 3,500 excluding tax per month. The total is EUR 11,000 excluding tax per month, and the whole of the French investigation is included in it rather than billed separately.

corps.b: The engagement moves to euros at par. What we discussed in Swiss francs becomes the same figure in euros. At today's European Central Bank rate, EUR 1 buys CHF 0.938, so CHF 7,500 is EUR 7,996. You therefore pay some EUR 500 a month less than the figure you accepted, and you carry no currency risk on a file denominated in Swiss francs.

Either letter may be terminated at the end of any month. At the end of the second month we review the scope and the fee together, in the light of what the searches have produced. If the French side proves empty, you will not be paying for it in month three.

corps.p: Each letter provides for a result fee of 10% excluding tax on what is actually recovered, payable only if sums or assets are in fact recovered.

On the French side one step can be taken almost at once. A request to the land registry gives the present owner of the Neuilly apartment and the whole chain of transfers, and it is open to any person, without having to establish one's capacity as an heir. It does not wait for the certificate of succession.

One thing is still outstanding, and it is the most urgent in the file. Please tell me the date on which you first learned of the CHF 302,870 balance, and how. A one year time limit runs from that date. I also need to know who signed the settlement agreement of 12 February 2025, and on what date, given that your father died during its negotiation.
Please return both letters signed, together with your full postal address, which I need in order to finalise them.
